# How is the rotation of the contact wrench cone specified when the feet are not aligned with the world frame in Crocoddyl?

> **Current answer:** The maintainer provides a single clear interface: the first parameter of the 'wrench cone constructor' defines the rotation. The thread does not provide information about the rotation matrix direction, reference frame convention, or re-validation code, so it can only be used as an entry point for localization, and cannot be directly used to construct the matrix from a picture alone.

## Key terms

- Rotation matrix (rotation matrix) (旋转矩阵)
- World frame (world frame) (世界坐标系)
- Support polygon (support polygon) (支撑多边形)
- Contact wrench cone (contact wrench cone) (接触力矩锥)

## Problem and symptoms

- Is the friction cone or CoP/ZMP cost sufficient for whole-body manipulation? When should the contact wrench cone be used instead?
- How should the wrench cone be oriented when the feet are not aligned with the world frame?
- The user cannot determine the relationship between the friction cone, CoP/ZMP cost, and the contact wrench cone in high dynamic whole-body operations.
- When the foot has a yaw angle, the user is unclear on how the wrench cone rotation matrix is defined.

## Environment

- Crocoddyl whole-body manipulation example, thread time from 2020-10 to 2021-02; no Crocoddyl version or robot model provided.

## Priority diagnostics

- The contact model requires separate checks for tangential friction, CoP support domain, and yaw torque boundary, rather than just seeing a friction cone and assuming full foot stability.
- The rotation parameter used in the wrench cone constructor must be verified and aligned with the actual foot direction.

## Possible causes

- The example was written before the contact wrench cone function was developed; the maintainer explained this is the example and it still uses the friction cone, not indicating that it is sufficient.

## Attempts

- The author checked the contact wrench cone paper and asked the maintainer if it also covers friction, ZMP/CoP, and yaw torque.
- The author provided an image of two feet not aligned with the world coordinate system and asked for the rotation matrix.

## Effective fixes

- A complete finite foot constraint requires using the contact wrench cone, and the friction cone or CoP cost should be removed to avoid duplication.
- When the foot is not aligned with the world frame, the first parameter of the wrench cone constructor should be used to specify the rotation.

## Result

- The author responded with clarification and stated they will update the example after the scheme is implemented; no further implementation or numerical results were provided.
- The rotation parameter issue is only mentioned by the maintainer in the interface, without any author verification.

## Limitations

- The thread does not provide specific API version, matrix direction, or code example for the contact wrench cone.
- It is not possible to derive the rotation matrix from a foot image alone; one must return to the target version and reference frame definition to construct the function.
- This discussion is from 2020/2021; the current Crocoddyl API name needs to be verified again.

## Safety notes

- In high dynamic real-world operations, both friction margin and CoP support domain should be monitored, and errors in the reference frame could result in seemingly feasible but unexecutable contact force moments.
